'''John Cedric Shepherdson''', [[Fellow of the British Academy|FBA]] (7 June 1926 – 8 January 2015) was a British logician who was [[Henry Overton Wills Professor of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Bristol]] from 1976 to 1991.

== Early life and education ==
Shepherdson was born in [[Huddersfield]] on 7 June 1926, the son of Arnold Shepherdson, a chemist, and his wife Elsie, née Aspinall. He attended [[Manchester Grammar School]] on a scholarship; excelling in mathematics, in 1943 he secured a state scholarship and an open scholarship to [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he read mathematics. He graduated with a first-class degree in 1946.<ref name="britac">John N. Crossley, [https://www.thebritishacademy.ac.uk/documents/1539/08-Shepherdson.pdf "John Cedric Shepherdson"], ''[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the British Academy]]'', vol. 15 (2016), pp. 141–160.</ref>

== Career and later life ==

Shepherdson was appointed to an assistant lectureship at the [[University of Bristol]] in 1946. He spent the rest of his career at the university, being promoted to lecturer in 1949, [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in 1955 and professor in 1964,<ref>Philip Welch, [https://web.archive.org/web/20230902152330/https://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2015/february/john-shepherdson.html "John Shepherdson, 1926–2015"], ''[[University of Bristol]]'', 10 February 2015. Archived from [https://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2015/february/john-shepherdson.html the original] on 2 September 2023.</ref> before he was finally [[Henry Overton Wills Professor of Mathematics]] from 1977 until he retired in 1991.<ref>[https://www.ukwhoswho.com/display/10.1093/ww/9780199540891.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-34658 "Shepherdson, Prof. John Cedric"], ''[[Who's Who (UK)|Who Was Who]]'' (online ed., [[Oxford University Press]], 2023). Retrieved 23 January 2024.</ref> He was elected a [[fellow of the British Academy]] in 1990.<ref>[https://www.thebritishacademy.ac.uk/deceased-fellows/?page=110 "Deceased Fellows"], ''British Academy''. Retrieved 23 January 2024.</ref>

Shepherdson was a keen climber and skier. His wife, Margaret, ''née'' Smith, a biochemist and academic whom he had married in 1955, died in 2014. Shepherdson died on 8 January 2015.<ref name="britac"/>
